lines.text: Since we discovered Pluto, it hasn't finished a single trip around the Sun.
And the date it finally will is wild.
Clyde Tombaugh found it in nineteen thirty, by flipping between two photos of the sky and spotting a dot that moved.
lines.caption: Clyde Tombaugh found it in 1930, by flipping between two photos of the sky and spotting a dot that moved.

lines.text: One lap around the Sun takes Pluto about two hundred and forty-eight years.
lines.caption: One lap around the Sun takes Pluto about 248 years.

lines.text: So far, it's made it less than halfway around.
Its first full lap since we found it ends on March twenty-third, twenty-one seventy-eight.
lines.caption: Its first full lap since we found it ends on March 23, 2178.

lines.text: Oh, and its name? Suggested by an eleven-year-old girl.
lines.caption: Oh, and its name? Suggested by an 11-year-old girl.
